title: Lip Sync
subtitle: Mouth shapes, listening, the jaw and full lines of dialogue

lessons.title: The Mouth Chart
lessons.summary: Eight mouths that cover almost every sound.

steps.title: Meet the mouths
steps.text: Say each sound out loud while you watch. Feel what your own mouth does.

beats.say: Here's the secret of lip sync. You don't draw letters, you draw sounds. And eight mouths cover nearly all of them.
Rest. Lips together and relaxed. This goes in the gaps between words.
A, like in cat or father. The jaw drops and the mouth opens wide. It's the biggest shape.
E, like in see. Wide and a bit flat, and you can see the top teeth.
O, like in go, is round and open. U, like in you, is the same idea, just smaller and tighter.
M, B and P press the lips together. You can't say them with your mouth open. Try it!
F and V tuck the top teeth onto the bottom lip. You can feel the air buzz.
And L lifts the tongue up behind the teeth. It works for T, D, N and TH too.
Grab a mirror and say each one. Every animator does this, even the pros.

steps.title: A
steps.text: Trace the A mouth: the jaw dropped, wide open.
steps.hint: The big open shape, the tongue at the bottom, and the line of the top teeth.

steps.title: M B P
steps.text: Trace the M B P mouth: lips pressed together.
steps.hint: The top lip, the bottom lip and the line where they meet.

steps.title: F V
steps.text: Trace the F V mouth: top teeth resting on the bottom lip.
steps.hint: The lip shape first, then the box of the teeth.

quiz.question: Which mouth do you use for the B in "ball"?
quiz.explain: M, B and P all start with the lips pressed shut.

lessons.title: Listen First
lessons.summary: Break a line into sounds and count the frames.

steps.title: Break down "Hello there"
steps.text: Each mouth is labelled with the sound it makes. The holds are counted at 12 frames a second.

beats.say: Before you draw a single mouth, listen. Let's break down, hello there.
Say it slowly. Hel, low, there. Now listen for the sounds, not the spelling.
He is an E sound. Then the L, which lifts the tongue. Then a big round O.
There starts with TH. The tongue touches the teeth, so we use the L mouth. Then E, held long.
Count the frames. At twelve frames a second, a quick sound gets two frames. A vowel you lean on gets five or six.
And there's a tiny rest between the words. Real speech has little gaps like that.
Pros write all this down on a chart before they animate. Sounds, then frames. Then drawings.

quiz.question: At 12 frames a second, how many frames is one second?
quiz.explain: 12 frames a second means 12 drawings, or holds, for every second.

quiz.question: The TH in "there" uses which mouth?
quiz.explain: The tongue touches the teeth, just like L, T, D and N.

quiz.question: Which sounds get held the longest?
choices: Vowels you lean on, like the O in hello
Quick sounds like T and K
quiz.explain: Vowels are the long, open sounds.

lessons.title: Say Hello
lessons.summary: Your first word, start to finish.

beats.say: Time for your first word. Hello! Watch and listen first.
It starts from rest. Then E for the he, nice and wide.
The L is quick. Just two frames with the tongue up.
Then the big O, held the longest. That's the part of the word you really hear.
And back to rest. Not too fast though, let the mouth close gently.

steps.title: Animate "hello"
steps.text: Five frames, holds already set. Draw the mouth on every frame over the guide, then press play.
steps.hint: E is wide and flat. L shows the tongue. O is round.
tips: Rest. A soft, closed mouth.
E, for the he. Wide and a bit flat, with the teeth showing.
L. Open a little and lift the tongue up behind the teeth.
O. A round, open mouth. This one's held the longest.
Rest again. Close the mouth gently. Now press play!

quiz.question: In "hello", which mouth is held the longest?
quiz.explain: The O is the long vowel you lean on.

lessons.title: The Jaw Drops
lessons.summary: Open sounds drop the whole jaw, not just the lips.

steps.title: Say "Wow, look"
steps.text: Watch the chin. It drops on the open sounds and comes back up on the closed ones.

beats.say: Here's something beginners miss. When you talk, your whole jaw moves, not just your lips. Let's say, wow, look.
Watch the chin. On the W, the lips push forward into a small U. The jaw barely moves.
Then the ow. The jaw drops right down for the big A. See the chin move?
Back up to a U for the end of wow. The jaw closes again.
Look starts with L, then a small oo, then the K closes it off.
Follow the dot. The jaw goes up and down with the sounds, like it's chewing the words.
If your lip sync looks like a puppet, check the jaw. A moving chin makes it feel real.

steps.title: Animate the jaw
steps.text: Eight frames, holds already set. On every frame, draw the jaw line and the mouth. The top of the head is already there.
steps.hint: Big open sounds drop the chin lower. Closed sounds bring it back up.
tips: Rest. The jaw closed, a relaxed mouth.
W. Lips pushed into a small round U. The chin hardly moves.
Ow. Drop the chin down and open the mouth wide for the A.
W again. Bring the chin back up to a small U.
A quick rest between the words.
L. A little open, with the tongue up.
Oo. A small round U, the chin nearly closed.
K, then rest. The jaw closes and the mouth relaxes.

quiz.question: On a big open sound like the A in "wow", the chin...
quiz.explain: Open vowels drop the whole jaw.

steps.title: Break down "I can draw!"
steps.text: A whole line of dialogue, sound by sound.

beats.say: Let's do a whole line. I can draw! Listen to it first.
I is really two sounds glued together. Ah, then ee. So that's an A, then a quick E.
Can. The C is a quick closed sound, just one frame. Then the A, and the N tucks into the next word.
Draw. The D lifts the tongue, the R pushes the lips into a small U, then a big open aw.
Draw is the important word, so it gets the biggest mouth and the longest hold. That's called an accent.
Then rest. Let the mouth close softly, and hold it so the line can land.

steps.title: Animate "I can draw!"
steps.text: Nine frames, holds already set. Draw the mouth on every frame, then press play and say it along with your animation.
steps.hint: A is wide open, E is wide and flat, L shows the tongue, U is small and round.
tips: Rest, before they speak.
Ah, the start of I. Open it wide.
Ee, the end of I. Wide and flat.
The C. Just one quick frame, nearly closed.
A, in can. Wide open again.
The N and D. Open a little, tongue up.
The R. Push the lips into a small round U.
Aw! The biggest, longest mouth. This is the accent.
Rest. Close it softly and hold.

quiz.question: The most important word in a line usually gets...
choices: The biggest mouth and the longest hold
quiz.explain: That's the accent: it's what the line is really about.

quiz.question: The word "I" is made of which two sounds?
